subject: Issues trying to learn secr coding to estimate fox densities

messages.author: d07eb249007ff7dc
messages.subject: Issues trying to learn secr coding to estimate fox densities
parts:
Hello, I'm really struggling to use secr to find fox densities from camera trap data. I am a beginner to RStudio. 

Currently, I seem to have read my capture and trap data in okay, using txt files. I ran read.capthist and for a change got no errors. Then I attempted to plot the capthist and it did it, but I thought it stange that when I plotted it, the data points are not on the detectors, is this right? 

I then copied and pasted some code for plotting a histogram of sucessive movement and it all came out as zero. I don't know whether any of the foxes were recorded on multiple cameras without looking but not sure if this would present a problem. When asking for a quick and biased estimate of sigma (which I don't understand) it also came out as zero. I tried fitting the model anyway using

fit <- secr.fit (sumbadsouth.secr, buffer = 1000 * initialsigma, trace = FALSE)

##resulting in the following:

Warning: no points in mask Warning in autoini(capthist = ch, mask = msk, binomN = tempbinomN, adjustg0 = details$binomN[1] == : 'dbar' close to zero; using detector spacing instead Warning: 'secr.fit' failed because initial values not found (data sparse?); specify transformed values in 'start'

I then copied and pasted code to create a mask:

```{r} Spiti.mask.sumbadsouth<-make.mask(traps(sumbadsouth.secr), buffer = 300, type = "trapbuffer") Spiti.sumbadsouth.hhn <- secr.fit(sumbadsouth.secr, model = list(D~1, lambda0~1, sigma~1), detectfn = "HHN", mask = Spiti.mask.sumbadsouth) ```

##resulting in the following:

Checking data Preparing detection design matrices Preparing density design matrix Finding initial parameter values...

Warning in autoini(capthist = ch, mask = msk, binomN = tempbinomN, adjustg0 = details$binomN[1] == : 'dbar' close to zero; using detector spacing instead Warning: 'secr.fit' failed because initial values not found (data sparse?); specify transformed values in 'start'

I also tried with 'detectfn = HN" and got another different error.

I really hope this doesn't mean I don't have enough data! Apologies for the long post, I'd be really grateful if someone could help.

Gaz

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Issues trying to learn secr coding to estimate fox densities
parts:
Without diving in too deeply -
My guess is this: 'secr' expresses all distances in metres. The plot method for capthist objects places the detections on successive occasions at a certain radial distance from the detector location (argument 'rad', default 5 ). This makes sense for  brushtail possums, but not for all other cases! Usually it just means rad is too small but if you have (i) expressed distances in km or (ii) failed to project data from lat-lon then you'll get strange results.
Murray
